title: Session invites: audit events and their own e-mail template
goal: Creating, accepting and revoking a session invite leave audit events like workspace invites do, and the invite mail says it is for one session only.
scope_in: `invite.create` (kind `session`, the role), `invite.accept` (user id and role) and `invite.revoke` events written in the background by the session invite service; the token is never in an event.
A `session_invite` e-mail template in @centcom/core (inviter, session name, role, link, expiry; every value escaped) used instead of the workspace invite template.
The event is built by one small pure function (`session-invite-audit.ts`) that never receives the token or the address.
A session invite revoked by someone other than its creator names the revoking user as the actor.
scope_out: Audit events for the key bundle routes.
build_against: The Postgres test database of B105's session invite tests and the in-memory e-mail service of B032's tests.
acceptance: Creating, accepting and revoking a session invite emits `invite.create`, `invite.accept` and `invite.revoke` with the actor, the workspace and the invite as target, and no token or address in the event (test).
The mail for a session invite uses the `session_invite` template with the session's name and the role; the HTML escapes the inviter and session names (test).
A revoke by a user other than the creator names that user as the actor (test).
An event never contains the invite token, its hash or the invited address (property test over random values).
An audit write that throws does not fail create, accept or revoke (test).
tests: session-invites.postgres.test.ts: the events and the mail parameters.
render.test.ts: the template and the registry's four templates.
session-invites.audit.test.ts: the event for each action; the actor of a revoke.
session-invites.audit.test.ts: a property test that no event holds the token, hash or address.
session-invites.audit.test.ts: a throwing emitter does not fail the request.
guardrails: MUST NOT put the invite token or the invited address in an audit event or a log line.
MUST write the events in the background: a slow or failing audit store never delays or fails an invite.
MUST use the existing `invite.*` actions (CT-API-AUDIT's list) with kind `session`, not new action names.
failure_modes: The audit write fails -> the request still succeeds (events are detached) and the failure is logged by the emitter.
The invited user is not the invite's address -> the accept is refused as before and no `invite.accept` event is written.
notes: Stacked after B105. Also changes (does not own) apps/api/src/modules/invites/{session-invites,routes}.ts, apps/api/src/collab.ts, packages/core/src/email/templates.ts and their tests (B105, B103, B032).
